page.title: Add a Dropbox destination
page.subtitle: Back up to Dropbox through the Dropbox API v2. Uses a long-lived access token from a Dropbox app.
page.registerHint: Save the credentials, then click Test connection to verify the round-trip.

help.accessToken: Generated access token from your Dropbox app. From the Dropbox App Console, open your app, then under Settings → Generated access token, click Generate. Stored encrypted at rest.
help.basePath: Optional folder inside Dropbox for backups, e.g. /Backups/2026. Leave blank to use the app root.

form.introBody: Generate a long-lived access token in the Dropbox App Console (your app → Settings → Generated access token). Paste it here. McHarbor stores the token encrypted at rest.
form.basePathHelp: Optional folder inside Dropbox for backups, e.g. /Backups/2026. Leave blank to use the app root. Not prefilled on purpose.

setup.title: Dropbox setup guide
setup.step1: In the Dropbox App Console, click Create app. Choose Scoped access (app folder or full Dropbox), pick Files and content read/write permissions, and pick a unique app name. Submit.
setup.step2: On the Permissions tab, enable the files.content.read and files.content.write scopes (plus any others your use case requires — these two are the minimum for backups). Click Submit to save.
setup.step3: On the Settings tab, scroll to Generated access token. Click Generate. Dropbox will show the token once — copy it now and paste it into the Access Token field on the left. McHarbor stores the token encrypted at rest.
setup.step4: Optional: set Base Path to a folder inside Dropbox where backups should land (e.g. /Backups/2026). Leave blank to use the app root (for App-folder apps) or your Dropbox root (for Full Dropbox apps). The form does not prefill a default.
setup.step5: Click Save. Then click Test connection in the storage card — McHarbor will round-trip a probe object, change it, and delete it.
setup.step6: Connect failed with "invalid_access_token"? The token may have expired or been revoked. Generate a fresh token in the Dropbox App Console and paste it again.
